notes.text: Kyle Palmieri is on injured reserve (knee injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Mathew Barzal has taken his spot beside Bo Horvat and Simon Holmström.

Ryan Pulock is out 1-2 weeks (upper body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. Matthew Schaefer has taken his spot beside Adam Pelech. That pair has had 40% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 36:02 together, about what it had with Pulock (43%).
Kyle Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 23 games, down from 37% last season.
They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen last game. Trevor Zegras takes shifts on two lines, L2 and L4. David Jiříček is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Seeler and York.
Owen Tippett is out (lower-body injury) and missed their last game.
David Jiříček has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 43% of the team’s power-play time in 11 games, up from 2% last season.

story.head: The Islanders’ defense joins the attack, the Flyers’ stays home
paras: The Islanders (12-8-5) lost 3-1 to Winnipeg last night, while the Flyers (10-12-6) beat Vancouver 5-2 the same night. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Islanders third (17th in the NHL) and the Flyers fifth (tied for 19th).
The Islanders’ record (.580) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.492), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Flyers’ record (.464) is about what their chances are worth.

The Islanders roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (1st). The Flyers play slow, tight games (2nd lowest), take away shots from the point (3rd lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (29th). The Isles’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Flyers’ not so much.

Matthew Schaefer (9 G / 17 A / 26 P in 25 GP) leads the Islanders in scoring, and Simon Holmström (10 G / 8 A / 18 P in 25 GP) has a team-high ten goals. For the Flyers, Matvei Michkov (11 G / 9 A / 20 P in 27 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Christian Dvorak (5 G / 12 A / 17 P in 28 GP) isn’t far behind.
Ilya Sorokin (10-5-2 / .916 SV% in 17 GS) has been outstanding for the Islanders and will likely start. Joseph Woll (5-7-2 / .886 SV% in 14 GS) is in line to start for Philadelphia.
